sentences.text: The present Misc. Appeal under section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act is filed against the award dated 1.07.2023 passed by III MACT, Ratlam in claim case No. 237/2021 whereby a sum of Rs.25,40,000/- has been awarded to the appellant Smt. Maya Kunwar along with interest as mentioned in para 36(2) of the impugned award.

Break-up of the amount awarded by the tribunal is as under :-
future loss of income Rs.21,59,136/- (Rs.8400/-x12+40%x90%x17) conveyance charges Rs.50,000/-
 special diet Rs.50,000/-
 physical pain Rs.80,000/-
 mental agony Rs.50,000/-
 future treatment expenses Rs.50,000/-
 loss of amenities Rs.50,000/-
 attendants charges Rs.50,000/-
2.

Facts of the case in brief are that on 24.2.2021 at abut 1.30 p.m. Jitendra Singh,
husband of appellant- Smt. Maya Kunwar and daughter Divyanshi were going from Jaora to Ratlam by motorcycle No. MP43 MC 9367, at that time tanker No. RJ09 JC 8390 which was driven by respondent No.1 rashly and negligently, collided with the motorcycle driven by husband of appellant and rear tyre of the tanker rolled over right hand and right leg of appellant, as a result right hand and right leg of the appellant was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35712 Maya Kunwar vs Ramkaran on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62694327/
1 2 MA-5158-2023 amputated.
3. Counsel for appellant submits that it is a case of 100% permanent disability but learned learned tribunal committed an error in assessing the same as 90%.
The appellant was doing the farming and milking the cows and also performed the household works, thereby she was earning Rs.9000/- per month.

Due to amputation, she is unable to perform her day-to-day work and also dependent on others and her future prospects have also been affected, therefore learned tribunal ought to have assessed the permanent disability as 100% and in other heads also the amount awarded is on lower side which deserves to be enhanced.
4. Learned counsel for respondent No.3 opposed the prayer by submitting that just and proper compensation has been awarded.

5. Taking into consideration that because of the accident, appellant suffered permanent disability which ought to have considered as 100% and it is not disputed that income of appellant was assessed as Rs.8400/- per month with 40% increase in the head of future prospects and in other heads also the amount awarded deserves to be enhanced.

In view of this Court, just and proper compensation will be computed as under :-
future loss of income Rs.23,99,040/- (Rs.8400/-x12+40%x100%x17) conveyance charges Rs.50,000/-
 special diet Rs.50,000/-
 physical pain Rs.1,00,000/-
 mental agony Rs.50,000/-
 future treatment expenses Rs.50,000/-
 loss of amenities Rs.50,000/-
 attendants charges Rs.1,50,000/-
loss of income during treatment period Rs.1,00,800/- (one year @ Rs.8400/-
p.m.x12) loss of expectation of life Rs.50,000/-
-------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------
total Rs.30,49,840/-
======================= ===================================
Thus, the appellant is entitled for a total sum of Rs.30,49,840/- instead of Rs.25,40,000/-.
The enhanced amount of Rs.5,09,840/- shall carry interest as awarded by the Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of the petition.
With the aforesaid, the appeal is allowed in part to the extent indicated NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35712 3 MA-5158-2023 hereinabove.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE MK Maya Kunwar vs Ramkaran on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62694327/
